body.objective: Add a fail-closed, content-addressed provenance-relock planner and transaction runner. The first consumer is sf:program/work/bridge-finite-harmonic-tier3-provenance-relock: one backward-compatible Lee-Wald component API change caused a multi-layer stale-hash cascade, and the resident Bridge team currently has to regenerate dozens of producer families in a shared dirty worktree before discovering the next stale frontier. Its first closure pass changed 230 JSON artifacts and found zero stale JSON consumers, yet the complete rail still returned 93 failures and 9 errors across 1,251 tests because already-modified consumers and Python-level hash gates were excluded. Certlab detects drift well but does not yet compute and execute the complete prospective-tree fixed point as one auditable migration.
body.stop_condition: Given a target certificate, paper gate or result set and a pinned input commit, materialize one isolated prospective tree and compute a least fixed point over: declared dependency_refs/source_manifests; nested certificate/schema/payload hashes; generated-artifact ownership; Python AST imports and literal/content-hash gates; verifier and test reads; code-read evidence edges; and every consumer already modified inside the candidate tree. Never exclude a consumer merely because it is dirty or already regenerated. Classify each edge as producer replay, independent verification, schema migration, test/verifier pin, paper citation, concurrent ownership conflict or unresolved/undeclared dependency. Before Tier 3, emit and verify a deterministic topological batch plan, exact closure digest, zero-stale-pin proof, changed-consumer census, ownership-conflict ledger, estimated cache hits and resource forecast. Execute batches in the isolated candidate tree, recomputing the closure after every generated change until both artifact bytes and the dependency graph reach a fixed point. Run producer and independent verifier rails separately; map any failing test to the smallest responsible dependency frontier; stop at the first semantic defect; and commit only a complete verified batch. Emit one migration receipt containing old/new hashes, commands, elapsed/resource data, cache keys, fixed-point iterations, changed paths, unresolved drift and proof that unrelated files were not mutated. Demonstrate the gate on the current Bridge fixture: the cheap preflight must predict or eliminate the stale causes behind the observed 93 failures and 9 errors before re-running the 1,251-test Tier-3 rail, then either relock the target completely or return the exact minimal semantic/ownership frontier.
body.forbid: no blind mass rewriting of hashes; no producer replay counted as independent verification; no mutation in the resident shared worktree; no broad git add; no partial downstream relock committed as if the target gate passed; no traversal based only on filename similarity; no undeclared code-read edge silently promoted to an authoritative dependency; no timeout or skipped verifier treated as pass; no paper theorem promotion by this tool
notes: The current Bridge run is an ideal acceptance fixture because the scoped theorem passes while the package-wide provenance closure is stale.
This should reuse Certlab, the evidence graph, staged-tree verification and content-addressed caches rather than create a separate migration system.
A dry-run plan is useful immediately even before transactional execution lands.

2026-07-20 Bridge acceptance evidence: the first scanner reported 230 changed JSON artifacts and zero stale downstream hashes. The completed active suite then reported 93 failures and 9 errors across 1,251 tests, with one opt-in heavy replay skipped. The Bridge agent traced these to stale producer/verifier pins and already-modified downstream artifacts excluded from the first closure, not to a scientific contradiction. This is the regression the fixed-point preflight must catch without first paying the full Tier-3 cost.

Long-term hygiene: new certificates and verifiers should emit machine-readable read/manifests so AST or literal-pin discovery is a corroborating migration path, not the permanent authority. A dependency-lint gate should refuse a content hash consumed by Python unless it is represented in the evidence graph or explicitly classified as an oracle-only test pin.

2026-07-21 Observer acceptance evidence: observer-tier3-provenance-fixed-point-relock-after-berger84-handoff has reached full-suite iteration 11 after repeatedly discovering one next stale descendant at a time. Each repaired frontier has retained byte-identical scientific payloads and changed only dependency/provenance pins; the current uninterrupted run crossed the previously failing positive-mixed component-jet frontier and passed 54% of the 1,300-plus Observer suite before this note. This is a second independent large-corpus reproduction of the same substrate gap: fail-fast Tier 3 is correctly safe, but without a prospective affected-consumer closure it spends tens of minutes per iteration and requires many serial replays to prove a provenance-only migration. Add this Observer chain as a CL2 acceptance fixture and require the dry-run planner to predict every one of its eleven known stale descendants from the initial Berger84 handoff change while preserving the producer/verifier separation and semantic-stop rule.
